answer: The protocol requires 1,000 unique location proofs to authenticate each agent by measuring signal transit via a fixed relay grid. An issuer assigns distinct spatial coordinates, and each signed receipt proves the agent occupied that site. A verifier reproduces the failure by re-running logs; any signal inlet discrepancy triggers an audit. An honest participant incurs linear travel costs, while an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes faces a gale of spatial congestion as the nadir of physical latency limits prevents spoofing.
